info.title: fff-server
info.description: Typed HTTP access to the fff file-search engine.

post.summary: Show how the parser decomposes a query, without searching anything.
post.description: Needs no workspace: parsing depends only on the preset.

Returns `201` when the index reached the requested readiness stage inside the block
budget, and `202` when it did not — the resource is returned either way, and a `202`
means poll `GET /v1/workspaces/{id}` rather than that anything failed.

202.description: Workspace still indexing; poll the resource

400.description: Root missing, not a directory, or too long

403.description: Root refused: filesystem/share root, or outside allowed_roots

409.description: Database already in use for this root

get.summary: Fetch one workspace, including current readiness. This is the poll target after a `202`.

delete.summary: Evict a workspace now, releasing its index, watcher threads and database handles.

post.description:
Worth calling after a commit or a branch switch: the watcher notices file changes, but
status is cached per file and a `git checkout` can change many at once.

post.summary: Literal glob match, frecency-ranked, bypassing the query parser.

get.summary: A previous query from this workspace's history, newest first.

400.description: No patterns, or a malformed cursor

post.description:
The automatic interval is derived from measured cost and can be up to 30 minutes on a
large share, so a client that knows it changed something should say so rather than wait.
Returns `202`: the rescan runs in the background, and the returned resource shows
`isScanning`.

503.description: Index not ready, or a rescan was throttled

post.summary: Fuzzy search over files and directories together.
Report that a file was opened.

400.description: Path missing or outside the workspace

post.summary: Report which result a query led to.

400.description: Path outside the workspace, or empty query

CasingDto.description:
Case handling. 0.11 replaced the old `smart_case` boolean with this; the boolean remains
only as a legacy fallback and is not offered here.

Unlike `matchType`, this is a real enum in the engine, so closing it in the contract is
safe and gives the C# client a proper enum.

ConstraintDto.description: One parsed constraint, as a discriminated union on `type`.

ConstraintType.description: What kind of thing a constraint constrains. Also the discriminator value.

CreateWorkspace.description: Per-workspace options, all defaulting from `[defaults]` in the config file.

aiMode.description:
`FFFMode::Ai` when true. Changes frecency decay, modification-score thresholds and
watcher event handling. Fixed for the workspace's life.

oneOf.description: Explicit content-cache budget. Omitted, fff sizes it from the file count.

contentIndexing.description:
Builds the bigram content index (~360 bytes/file). Required for typo-resistant and
fuzzy grep. Measured at roughly 20x the cost of the directory walk.

oneOf.description: Ranking boost for files in recent commits on the current branch.

root.description:
Path to index. Any spelling; it is canonicalised and deduplicated by filesystem
identity, so a UNC path and a mapped drive pointing at one directory give one
workspace.

waitFor.description: Which readiness stage to block for.

watch.description: Background filesystem watcher. Verified working over SMB (~500ms).

maxAccessFrecency.description: Highest access-frecency score among the files beneath it.

EffectiveOptions.description:
The settings a workspace was actually created with, echoed back so a client never has to
guess which defaults applied.

negated.description: True when the constraint was negated, as in `!tests/`.

ExtensionConstraint.description: A file extension, without a dot.

negated.description: True when the constraint was negated, as in `!tests/`.

absolutePath.description:
Native separators, and free of any `\\?\` prefix — so it is safe to open and safe to
display. Not an identity key.

directory.description: Parent directory, with a trailing `/`. Empty at the root.

gitRecencyScore.description:
Boost from recent commits on the current branch. Reported separately because
`totalFrecencyScore` does **not** include it, so it would otherwise be invisible.

relativePath.description:
Repo-relative, **forward slashes on every platform**, carrying on-disk casing. This
is what the engine stores and what globs and path constraints match against.

totalFrecencyScore.description:
Access plus modification only — deliberately excluding `gitRecencyScore`, matching
the engine's own `total_frecency_score()`.

negated.description: True when the constraint was negated, as in `!tests/`.

FileTypeConstraint.description: One of the engine's file-type names, e.g. `rust`.

negated.description: True when the constraint was negated, as in `!tests/`.

maxCommits.description: Commits to look back over. fff caps this at 128 internally.

maxFilesPerCommit.description:
Commits touching more files than this are ignored, so a sweeping commit does not
boost the whole tree.

GitStatus.description:
Git status, in full.

`git2::Status` is a bitflags value — a file can be staged-modified *and* worktree-modified
at once. Every other fff binding flattens it to one string and loses that, so both forms
are emitted: `status` for convenience, `flags` for fidelity.

flags.description: Every set bit, so a client can see combinations the single label hides.

GitStatusConstraint.description: Git status filter, mirroring the engine's four categories.

negated.description: True when the constraint was negated, as in `!tests/`.

GitStatusValue.description: The git status categories the engine can filter on.

GlobConstraint.description: A glob pattern. Forward slashes only.

negated.description: True when the constraint was negated, as in `!tests/`.

GlobRequest.description:
Glob-only request. Bypasses the query parser entirely: the pattern is used literally,
results are frecency-ranked. Use it when the pattern is already a glob and fuzzy
matching on top would only add noise.

pattern.description: Forward slashes only — the matcher does not treat `\` as a separator.

byteOffset.description:
Byte offset of this line within the file. Stays a byte count, because that is what it
is for: seeking directly to the line.

colUtf16.description: Column of the first match on this line, in **UTF-16 code units** into `lineContent`.

fileIndex.description:
Index into the response's `files` array. Kept as an index rather than embedding the
file, so a file's metadata is not repeated across hundreds of matches within it.

matchRangesUtf16.description:
Every match on this line, in UTF-16 code units into `lineContent`. The MCP server
uses these only to centre its truncation window and never emits them.

GrepPreset.description: Which parser preset to read constraint tokens with.

classifyDefinitions.description: Tags lines that look like definitions. Roughly 2% overhead.

cursor.description: Continuation token from a previous response's `nextCursor`.

enforceTimeBudget.description:
Apply the budget even before anything has matched. Off by default, matching the
engine: a zero-match query otherwise scans everything.

pageSize.description: Soft cap on matches per response; the engine finishes the file it is in.

query.description:
Pattern plus optional constraint tokens, e.g. `*.rs !tests/ TODO`. Passed to the
engine byte-for-byte: backslashes are **not** folded, because a backslash is
legitimate content in a pattern.

timeBudgetMs.description:
Milliseconds before returning partial results. 0, the default, means unbounded.
Grep over SMB measured ~7 ms/file, so a full 87k-file tree is around ten minutes: a
budget here is a real safeguard, but one that silently truncates, which is why
cursor paging is the better tool.

trimWhitespace.description:
Strips leading whitespace from matched and context lines, adjusting the reported
offsets accordingly.

aborted.description:
True when the engine's abort signal was tripped, which currently means the client
disconnected mid-search. Results are partial.

Note this does **not** cover a `timeBudgetMs` truncation: the engine reports that by
returning early with a non-null `nextCursor` and no separate flag, so a client that
cares about completeness should page until `nextCursor` is null rather than trust
this field alone.

filteredFileCount.description: Files eligible after filtering out binaries, oversized files and constraint misses.

literalFallback.description:
True when a constrained query found nothing and the engine retried the whole raw
query as literal text, ignoring the constraints it had inferred.

mode.description: The mode actually used, after `auto` resolution.

nextCursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page. `null` means the search is exhausted.

regexFallbackError.description:
Set when a regex failed to compile and the search fell back to literal matching.
The request still succeeds; this explains why the results look literal.

totalFilesSearched.description: Files actually searched in this call.

Health.description: Server liveness and, once the pool exists, per-workspace readiness.

engineVersion.description: The `fff-search` release this binary is built against.

status.description: Always `"ok"` when the process is answering.

workspaceCount.description: Number of live workspaces in the pool.

HistoryResponse.description: A query from this workspace's history.

query.description: `null` when the history is shorter than the requested offset.

LocationDto.description:
A `file.ts:42:10` suffix parsed out of the query. The MCP server discards this entirely.

`line` is always present; `col`, `endLine` and `endCol` depend on `type`.

LocationType.description: Which kind of location a query specified.

MixedDirectoryHit.description: A directory from a mixed search.

MixedFileHit.description: A file from a mixed search.

MixedHit.description: A hit from a mixed search: a file or a directory, distinguished by `type`.

MixedKind.description: Whether a mixed hit is a file or a directory.

MultiGrepRequest.description:
Multi-pattern search: any pattern matching counts, via SIMD Aho-Corasick. Faster than
regex alternation and much faster than N separate searches. Always literal text.

constraints.description: Constraint tokens only — no pattern text. e.g. `*.rs !tests/`.

ParsePreset.description:
Which preset to parse with. The presets differ in which constraint kinds they recognise,
so the same string can mean different things.

ParseQueryResponse.description:
How the parser decomposed a query.

Exists because the DSL is powerful and silent about mistakes: a token that looks like a
glob but is not recognised as one simply becomes fuzzy text, and the results still look
plausible. This endpoint makes that visible from the client side.

fuzzyParts.description: The fuzzy terms left after constraints were removed.

grepText.description: What grep would search for: the query minus constraint tokens.

warnings.description: Problems that would otherwise pass unnoticed.

PartsConstraint.description: Several text parts, all of which must match.

negated.description: True when the constraint was negated, as in `!tests/`.

PathSegmentConstraint.description: A path segment a result must sit under.

negated.description: True when the constraint was negated, as in `!tests/`.

Problem.description:
RFC 9457 problem details. ASP.NET Core deserialises this into `ProblemDetails` with no
client-side code.

Clients switch on `code`, never on `detail`: `code` is a stable identifier, `detail` is
prose from the engine and may change between fff releases.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code. Switch on this.

detail.description: Prose explanation for this occurrence. Not stable; do not parse.

status.description: HTTP status code, repeated here as RFC 9457 specifies.

title.description: Short, human-readable summary of the error class.

type.description: Stable URN identifying the error class.

ScoreDto.description: The complete score breakdown: all 13 fields the engine computes.

gitRecencyBoost.description: Added in fff 0.11; absent from every other binding.

gitStatusBoost.description: Dropped by the C ABI and by the TypeScript SDK.

matchType.description:
Documented as an **open** string, not a closed enum: it is a bare `&'static str` in
the engine with no enum backing it, so a future value must not break a client.
Known values include `fuzzy`, `fuzzy_filename`, `exact`, `prefix`, `path`.

SearchHit.description:
One file hit, with its score and match highlighting.

The engine returns items, scores and match offsets as three parallel arrays; they are
zipped here. Nothing is lost, and a generated C# client is far better for it.

matchRangesUtf16.description:
Which parts of `item.relativePath` matched, in UTF-16 code units. The MCP server
discards this information entirely.

SearchRequest.description:
Search request. Supply `query`, or `structured`, or neither (an empty query ranks the
whole index by frecency). Supplying both is rejected rather than silently preferring one.

comboBoostMultiplier.description:
Query-history combo boost. Only has an effect once a client reports selections via
`track-query`.

currentFile.description:
A path to deprioritise, so the file a caller is already looking at does not dominate
its own results. Also feeds the distance bonus for nearby paths.

query.description:
The raw fff query DSL, e.g. `git:modified src/**/*.rs !tests/ user controller`.
Passed to the engine byte-for-byte. Glob separators must be `/`.

oneOf.description: Constraints as data, instead of a DSL string.
A `file.ts:42:10` suffix parsed out of the query, if present.

totalMatched.description: Matches across the whole index, not just this page.

warnings.description:
Non-fatal notes about the query — currently backslashes in glob-looking tokens,
which would otherwise match nothing with no explanation.

StructuredQuery.description:
Constraints as data, for clients that would rather not build DSL strings.

Separators are folded in `globs`, `pathSegments`, `filePaths` and `excludePathSegments`,
where a separator is unambiguously a separator. The engine's glob backend treats **only**
`/` as a separator, so without folding `src\**\*.rs` would not be applied as a glob at
all — it would fall through to fuzzy text matching and quietly return unrelated results.

fuzzy.description: Free-text fuzzy terms. Split on whitespace into parts, as the DSL parser would.

pathSegments.description: Path segments a result must contain, e.g. `src`.

text.description: Literal text a path must contain.

TextConstraint.description: Literal text a path must contain.

negated.description: True when the constraint was negated, as in `!tests/`.

TrackAccessRequest.description:
Report that a file was opened, so its access-frecency score rises.

This is the half of frecency a REST server cannot observe for itself. The modification
half is computed from mtime and git status and works unaided; the access half needs a
client to say what was actually opened. A client that never calls this loses nothing
relative to running without the databases.

path.description:
Repo-relative (forward or back slashes) or absolute. Must resolve inside the
workspace root.

accessCount.description: Times this file has been reported, after this call.

relativePath.description: The path as recorded, repo-relative with forward slashes.

TrackQueryRequest.description:
Report which result a query led to, feeding the combo boost.

The boost only fires once the same (query, file) pair has been reported
`minComboCount` times (default 3), so a single call changes nothing visible.

selectedPath.description: The file the client acted on. Repo-relative or absolute.

Utf16Range.description:
A half-open range of **UTF-16 code units**.

The engine produces UTF-8 byte offsets. Those are converted here because .NET strings
are UTF-16: a byte offset would silently address the wrong characters on any line
containing non-ASCII, and the point of this API is that the client does no
post-processing.

WaitFor.description: How far creation should block before answering.

WorkspaceResource.description: A workspace as clients see it.

gitRoot.description: Git worktree root, if one was discovered.

id.description:
Stable identifier, derived from the directory's filesystem identity. Re-creating the
same root — under any spelling, and across server restarts — returns this same id.

isNetworkPath.description:
True when the root resolved to a UNC path, mapped drives included. Reported for
visibility only: freshness and eviction key off measured cost, not path type.

isWarmupComplete.description:
The content index is built. Fuzzy grep needs this, and the watcher is installed only
after it completes.

options.description: The settings this workspace was actually built with.

rescanIntervalSecs.description: Effective automatic rescan interval, derived from `timeToReadyMs`.

root.description:
The resolved root, with any verbatim `\\?\` prefix stripped. Display-and-open safe;
not an identity key.

scannedFilesCount.description: Files seen by the most recent scan.

timeToReadyMs.description:
Observed time from construction until content indexing first completed. While the
workspace is still warming, this is elapsed time so far.

WorkspaceStatus.description: Readiness, as a single field a client can branch on.
